newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Nov durable goods fell 1.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Nov durable goods fell 1.6 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported November orders for durable goods fell 1.6 percent compared to a revised 0.5-percent increase in October.

ALLAN LESLIE, INDEPENDENT ECONOMIST, NEW YORK: "I believe the underlying trend continues to move along albeit at not quite as fast a pace (as in recent months.) ... We continue this trend of upward increases in quarters ... which is what the Federal Resereve wants to see."

DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "The durables are weak, but the jobless claims drop shows more strength in the labor market. The two end up offsetting each other. "The durables weakness ex-transport can be seen as a correction from October. People were expecting a rebound in transport orders after the weakness last month. The transport figures are looking a little weak, but the weakness ex-transport is a correction from a strong gain last month. "I don't think there's going to be any major bond (market) reaction to these figures," Sloan added.

The Labor Department released new filings for state unemployment benefits in the latest week at 0830 EST/1330 GMT as well. Claims totaled 335,000 in the week ended December 21 compared to a 350,000-claim tally in the prior week.

ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "It was electrical machinery that collapsed 9.3 percent ... some of this because last month was so strong for some of these numbers that you had to have some reversal, like electrical machinery."

Adolfson continued: "Remember (electrical machinery) was up 16.9 percent the prior month, so a decline of 9.3 percent is not surprising. It is definitely not a strong number ... manufacturing is still struggling."

KEVIN FLANAGAN, MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST AT DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "It was right in line with our expectations. The (Treasury) market may do a little bit better, but I wouldn't expect any sort of a breakout as a result of the numbers.
"We also didn't get any strength or input from the transportation sector," he added.

JAMES PADINHA, ECONOMIST, MMS INTERNATIONAL INC: "Overall it's a pretty weak report. There was a little retracement in the electrical category -- it was up about 17 percent in October and that came off about 9.0 percent, so that's why the number came in so much lower than people thought.

"That, in itself, is enough to give weakness, but people also look at non-defense capital goods and that ex-aircraft which was down 1.6, so it's negative, but not weak enough to label the whole sector weak in the fourth quarter.
"We're up 4.5 percent in September and another 0.5 in October, so even the November decline doesn't erase that."
